stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to use spontaneous fine distinction to synthesize and reformulate ideas related to explaining subtle differences with appropriate C2 complexity. The central language focus is spontaneous fine distinction. In the context of mastery of flexible communication, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At C2 content level, control comes from flexible choices rather than rare vocabulary. Preserve subtle meaning while reframing, compressing, expanding, or shifting register, and make rhetorical effects deliberate rather than decorative.

blocks.text: Start with the model “The discussion highlighted draw on analogy.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “A clear explanation addresses subtle difference directly.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: spontaneous fine distinction. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by spontaneous fine distinction; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For explaining subtle differences, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.
